turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_retention_train.csv: 55 real samples, columns
    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,
    Al, Cu, W, S) and `target` (the measured hot-strength retention ratio
    YS(600C)/YS(20C)).
  - b3_htsteel_retention_pool.csv: 26 CANDIDATE samples whose hot-strength
    retention ratio YS(600C)/YS(20C) was NOT measured, columns
    `candidate_id` and the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST hot-
strength retention ratio YS(600C)/YS(20C), then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
# Analysis

Looking at the training data, the samples with the **highest retention ratios** (target > 0.8) share a very distinctive composition signature:

| Fe | Cr | Ni | Ti | Al | W | target |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 42.28 | 15.0 | 36.0 | 1.30 | 0.00 | 3.15 | **1.000** |
| 41.15 | 15.0 | 36.3 | 0.78 | 1.09 | 3.58 | **0.875** |
| 50.55 | 15.1 | 26.9 | 1.16 | 1.23 | 2.97 | **0.821** |
| 60.47 | 11.25| 23.0 | 2.90 | 0.40 | 0.00 | **0.903** |

Key pattern: **high Ni (20–36%) combined with Ti (1–3%) and/or W (2.4–3.6%) and Al (0.4–1.2%)** strongly boosts high-temperature strength retention — likely due to Ni-stabilized austenite plus Ti/Al intermetallic (γ′-type) precipitation and W solid-solution strengthening, which resist softening at 600°C much better than simple Cr–Ni stainless matrices.

Scanning the candidate pool for the closest matches to this high-retention signature:

- **c019** (Fe41.6, Cr15, Ni35, Ti2.8, Al1.05, W3.2) — near-identical to the target=1.0 and 0.875 champions, with even higher Ti.
- **c013** (Fe47.4, Cr15.1, Ni27.5, Ti1.16, Al1.05, W2.4, +Mo2.5) — closely matches the 0.82–0.875 samples.
- **c004** (Fe51.4, Cr15.2, Ni26, Ti1.2, Al1.2, +Mo2.9) — near-duplicate of the 0.821 sample.
- **c011** (Fe63.4, Cr11.25, Ni19.5, Ti2.9, Al0.8) — matches the 0.903 sample profile closely.
- **c008** (Fe60.7, Cr14, Ni19, Nb1.1, W2.4, B0.005) — nearly identical to a training row with target ≈0.696, the next-best realistic match after the Ti/Al/W/Ni cluster.

Lower-Ni austenitic (Cr18/Ni9-10, no Ti/Al/W) and plain low-alloy ferritic samples in the pool consistently map to mid/low targets (0.3–0.7) in the training set, so they were ranked below these five.

**Final: c019, c013, c004, c011, c008**
